verdict.probe_answer: Both arms remove the per-param ordinal collision at the root with a single ordered binding pass and add a regression that would fail on the buggy code. Arm A is narrower and pins the serialized scope-graph BindingRef directly. Arm B also fixes the bug, but through a broader add_locals signature refactor and a less direct resolution-based ordinal test. Both fixes appear inert beyond the intended repair.
verdict.rationale:
WRONG: No demonstrated blocker in either arm. Both preserve ordinal enumeration over the full parameter list and attach LocalFact by def_byte.

SMELL: Arm B has more churn than needed, changing add_locals and all local binding call sites. It appears behavior-preserving, but it increases review surface relative to Arm A.

SMELL: Arm B's ordinal regression checks resolved use-site candidates rather than directly inspecting scope-graph bindings. It should still fail on the buggy code, but Arm A's test more directly enforces the Phase-1 inertness contract.

Arm A is materially better because it is the smaller scoped repair and its regression directly asserts the serialized BindingRef ordinals.
